label: July 1917
headline: A New Gas
deck: Mustard gas burns the defenders of Ypres; the German Chancellor falls
caption: Men with bandaged eyes wait in line at a dressing station
body: On the night of 12 July German shells fall on the British lines around Ypres with a new gas. It smells faintly of mustard, its effect comes hours later, and it lingers in the ground for days: the skin blisters, the eyes swell shut, the lungs burn. Masks protect the face, not the body.

In Berlin, on 13 July, Chancellor Bethmann Hollweg resigns, pressed out by the army command and the Reichstag alike. Georg Michaelis, a Prussian official little known outside the ministries, succeeds him.
In Arabia, Arab forces under Auda abu Tayi take the port of Aqaba from the landward side on 6 July, after a long march through the desert; the Arab revolt now has a harbour on the Red Sea.
In Petrograd armed demonstrations against the war are put down in mid-July, and Kerensky becomes prime minister.
briefs: Britain's royal family takes the name of Windsor
Greece enters the war on the side of the Entente
Serbs, Croats and Slovenes agree at Corfu on a common state
